correctness.rationale: Writing each binary bit as (1+ε_i)/2 gives precisely h(u)=2^(d−2) E|m+X| with m=Σu_i and X=Σu_i ε_i. Reflection of X gives E|m+X|=E max(|m|,|X|). Theorem 7 of De–Diakonikolas–Servedio provides the sharp first-moment inequality and exact two-coordinate equal-magnitude equality condition. Equal signs fail to achieve equality for the shifted expectation because X=0 on a positive-probability event and m≠0; unequal signs have m=0. Thus the only unit equality normals are (e_i−e_j)/√2 for ordered i≠j. The centered inscribed radius is the minimum support and is also globally optimal: the paired opposite support constraints would bound any translated ball by the same radius. Each minimizing normal annihilates binary generators with b_i=b_j, spanning the entire hyperplane (via e_i+e_j and remaining basis vectors). The supporting face is exactly the zonotope of these free summands, translated by the fixed endpoints of the other summands, and deleting the duplicated coordinate gives the smaller White Whale with the stated √2 stretch. Its tangent point is in the facet interior since a second supporting facet there would also be tangent to the smooth ball at the same point and therefore have the same normal. The two opposing ball constraints force c_i=c_j for all optimal centers. Every other facet has strictly positive slack at zero, and there are finitely many, so a nonzero diagonal interval remains feasible; symmetry, convexity and compactness make this the claimed segment. Every coordinate is bounded by 2^(d−2), and all-plus and all-minus choices attain the antipodal cube corners. Any mixed-sign corner would force the segment generated by e_i+e_j to its two different endpoints, which is impossible. The two antipodes alone force the unique enclosing ball of radius 2^(d−2)√d. This fully checks d≥2, including the embedded one-dimensional facet model when d=2. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its cofactor code uses rounded floating-point determinants followed by exact integer support comparisons, and its sampled stresses are not an all-dimensional argument.

evidence: General centered zonotope radius extrema are signed sums of generators and minima of sums of absolute projections. Sharp L¹ Khintchine with exact equality is known for the unshifted sign sum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior extrema formulas require solving the instance; they do not state its equality cases. The unshifted inequality's same-sign equality cases must be eliminated for the binary support, and polytope faces and the feasible-center locus must then be determined geometrically.

evidence: The outer radius is an elementary evaluation of known signed-sum optimization using the common octant of the generators. Applying Khintchine after symmetrization gives the lower bound and candidate inner equality directions. Generators with equal chosen bits, and finiteness of the remaining facet constraints, give additional structural conclusions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the existing metric formulas and sharp sign inequality wholesale; radius evaluations alone are not the reason for accepting this record. Prior statements inspected do not give the full family-specific shell, its embedded-facet recursion, and the nonunique center structure together before this record.

The zonotope, the general radius formulas and the sharp Khintchine inequality/equality statement are prior results. A directly overlapping White Whale Resultary record dated Nov 8 gives the same inradius, minimizing facet directions and entire center segment with additional endpoint information. This is substantial exact overlap, but not evidence of previously published coverage of the Oct 18 finding on the available record dates. value.rationale: The exact nearest facets and all optimal centers are natural invariants for a family whose total face complexity grows rapidly. Knowing that the nearest shell only has quadratic size, identifying its lower-dimensional copies, and proving a one-dimensional set of maximal-ball centers distinguish the geometry from a mere radius evaluation. The probabilistic equality condition provides a concise route to this geometric structure and the result is for every dimension in the natural family; no center endpoint formula is claimed.
